cells.tense: You're standing in what hasn't settled yet, and you're steady right there.
cells.ask: Pick up the one heavy thing you've been walking around today, put it where it belongs, and let that be the whole of it.
cells.core:
Nothing here has locked into a plan, and you can bear what's unformed without forcing it into shape. Weight doesn't rattle you and doesn't need a name before you'll lift it. You can sort what's actually in your hands from what you're only imagining will land there. That steadiness is what keeps the open space open — and it's the kind of strength that never needed an audience to hold.

Do one physical thing that asks only for your arms and today. Pick up what you've been stepping past, or set down what you've been holding past the point it was ever yours. Whatever your hands do today stays done, and you'll know something about yourself just by having done it.

cells.tense: You're already lifting a weight that hasn't arrived, and your shoulders know it.
cells.ask: Write down one load you're braced for that nobody has handed you, and leave it on the page for the rest of today.
cells.core:
Ahead of you sits a day when the holding will matter, and you've stepped into that day already. Readiness helps when there's something real to brace against. What's on you is bracing without the weight, so the strength spends itself on a scene that hasn't shown up. The strength is real. It's just arriving early to a job that isn't open yet.

Write the load down that wasn't actually handed to you, and let the page hold it until tomorrow. Strength that shares can find the one thing that isn't yours to lift alone and hand it back to whoever it belongs to. You can pick it up again if it turns out to be yours, and you'll have lost nothing by setting it down for a day.

cells.tense: You're standing just past a threshold, with strength in you that you've stopped taking up.
cells.ask: Say out loud, to one person or to a page, one thing you carried that nobody saw you carry.
cells.core:
There's strength in the room and it isn't being used. Not because it went anywhere — because picking things up stopped feeling like something to do. Used well, weight gets set down once the work is finished. Lately the setting-down doesn't happen, so your arms stay full long after the day ends. The strength hasn't gone anywhere, and it isn't asking to be proven.

Let one thing you carried be known — spoken or written, one sentence, today. Someone hearing what you did alone lets the load finish and your arms finally empty. Small and private is enough. The next thing you lift can be lifted later, and today's telling commits you to nothing more.

cells.tense: You're already holding weight in this open space, and you're calling it something else.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been calling the situation, and say it once as something you're choosing to carry.
cells.core:
You're doing the strength already — quietly, without a scene, in the unmade part of a day — but the story you tell has the strength coming from somewhere other than you. Done well, this holding is known as a choice. As it stands, the choice is real and unreported, so the day keeps doing the lifting while you keep saying you're just getting through.

Smaller than the strength: one plain sentence, in your own words, about one thing you're holding that is actually yours to hold. Say it today. The hoping kind of strength builds from noticing what's already been made, and one sentence is enough to start noticing.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person is 'the one deciding what gets passed on' — the record only says Steadfastness is present, not that they are authoring it. A reader might say 'I'm not in Potential, I'm just trying to get through a hard week.' The asks survive being wrong because they are small, physical, and testable today — each teaches something even if the read is off. The sentence 'Without the choosing, the carrying is just carrying' serves the writer's love of the aphorism more than the reader; I've cut it and kept the plain condition in its place.
